overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving insufficiently detailed minutes for five executive sessions (Nov. 24, Dec. 3, Dec. 14, Dec. 28, 2021; Jan. 11, 2022), but not for the Jan. 25, 2022 session, and no intentional violation was found.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board approved insufficiently detailed minutes for executive sessions held Nov. 24, Dec. 3, Dec. 14, and Dec. 28, 2021, and Jan. 11, 2022.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law requires that meeting minutes include more than a statement that a public body discussed a specified topic; the Law requires that the minutes summarize the discussion that was held.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Jan. 25, 2022 executive session minutes were insufficiently detailed because they only said the Board 'discussed' a police chief vacancy advertising process.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law with respect to the January 25, 2022, minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session minutes were insufficiently detailed because they omitted the time the executive session started.
allegations.key_passage: We have not construed the Open Meeting Law as requiring meeting minutes to separately list the start time of an executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's minutes violations were intentional under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find no evidence that the Board intentionally violated the Law or acted with deliberate ignorance of the Law's requirements.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent.

Amend, to the best of its ability, the executive session minutes for Nov. 24, Dec. 3, Dec. 14, and Dec. 28, 2021, and Jan. 11, 2022, and release them to the public unless lawfully withheld under G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f).
Certify compliance to the Division within 45 days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
